body: Why add new file instead of using `test_packed_scene.cpp`?

```suggestion
	void _parse_nodes(const Ref<PackedScene> &p_current_scene, cost Ref<FileAccess> &p_file);
```
(or without const if not applicable)
Why are you setting this to null if it's the method's argument?

I am used to C#, where if you have a ref, and you set it to null, the reference is set to null also outside of the function. My brain probably just crossed the wires when I had to refactor this function to set directly `packed_scene` from the class body, but then I had to change again to the way it is now :upside_down_face: 

In this case it's best to just return the scene and set like it was before, right?

`Ref<>` is just a Godot's wrapper for RefCounted objects.
If you want to pass it as a modifiable reference, you can change the parameter to `Ref<PackedScene> &r_current_scene` (i.e. with `&`).

Because resources also have a dedicated file for save and load testing, but since I wanted to make a new PR extending from new one. The file was getting quite big, so I separated the save and load of scenes.

In this PR is also already quite big.
